subject: Plain-language DPA + transfer summary for sales one-pager
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Plain-language DPA + transfer summary for sales one-pager

Team —

We need a concise, public-facing summary of the DPA and cross-border data transfer posture that the sales team can send to prospects (starting with Acme). Goal: one A4 / single-slide one-pager and a short FAQ (3–5 Qs) for SDRs. Key asks:
- Short explanation of what data we collect/retain during hosted API calls (hosted inference).
- Where data may be stored/transferred and the safeguards (SCCs / adequate safeguards / KMS).
- Clear line about subprocessors and how customers can get the current subprocessors list.
- A short, plain-language note about logging, retention windows, and how customers can request deletion.

Can Laura take first pass? Kimberly and Marcus, please flag anything that is legally or product-sensitive we must avoid in public copy. I want a draft by EOD PT tomorrow. Acme legal has already asked for a short summary in plain terms, so we should aim for consumer-friendly wording without losing accuracy.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none in this message

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T15:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plain-language DPA + transfer summary for sales one-pager

Hi Naomi —

Attached is a first draft: redwood_dpa_plainlang_v1.docx (summary + 5-question FAQ). I focused on short sentences and avoided legalese. Highlights:
- "What we process": brief bullets saying we process request content to generate responses and store minimal logs for diagnostics and billing.
- "Where data goes": list of regions (US, EU via regional hosting, APAC partners) and an explanation that some metadata may be routed to partner infra.
- "Subprocessors": one-liner + link to full subprocessors map (Drive link placeholder).
- "Retention": default 30 days for logs + configurable retention for Dedicated/Private.

Open issues I flagged in the doc for product/legal:
1) We used "we may transfer data to service providers outside your region" — is that okay to leave without mentioning SCCs?
2) I wrote "we use encryption at rest and in transit" — Marcus, can you confirm KMS/HSM language?

If this looks good I can produce a sales-friendly PDF and a short script for SDRs.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Writer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa_plainlang_v1.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-13T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plain-language DPA + transfer summary for sales one-pager

Thanks Laura — solid start. A few concrete edits and flags below (I also attached Acme's initial questionnaire so we can align): acme_questions.xlsx

Edits / flags:
- Subprocessors: please replace any ambiguous "may" language with a clear process: "We maintain an up-to-date subprocessors list; customers can request the list or view it here. We notify customers of changes per the DPA." That avoids implying arbitrary transfers.
- Data transfers: mention SCCs or other transfer mechanisms explicitly for EU→US transfers. Saying "we may transfer" without adequate safeguards will trigger more follow-ups.
- Retention: avoid a hard default number in the public one-pager; instead give a typical retention window (e.g., "typically 30 days for diagnostic logs; enterprise customers can configure or contract different retention policies").
- Encryption/KMS: confirm we can say "customer data encrypted at rest and in transit; keys managed with industry-standard KMS; optional customer-managed keys for Private deployments." Marcus, is that accurate?

Also propose a tiny FAQ entry on "How do I get the current subprocessors list?" that links to a short self-serve page plus an email contact.

Kimberly Park
Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_questions.xlsx

From: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@acme-corp.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-14T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Plain-language DPA + transfer summary for sales one-pager

Thanks Naomi and team — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from Acme Legal after a quick read:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood signs standard SCCs or if you rely on another mechanism for EU→US transfers? If SCCs, are they attached to the DPA or handled via an addendum?
2) For subprocessors: will Acme get advance notice of onboarding new subprocessors and a window to object?
3) Regarding logs: can you provide the schema for the diagnostic logs (fields only) and an example retention policy for Hosted API (not Dedicated)?

If you prefer, we can take the one-pager and insert our own contract references, but it helps to have the exact wording you intend to share publicly.

Best —
Sarah Klein
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud
